name: Energy
blurb: Tái tạo, nhiên liệu hoá thạch, tiết kiệm điện

words.definitionEn: capable of being replenished naturally
words.example: Many countries are investing in renewable energy sources.

words.definitionEn: relating to the sun
words.example: Solar panels convert sunlight into electricity.

words.definitionEn: natural movement of air used for energy
words.example: Wind turbines generate electricity from wind.

words.definitionEn: generating electricity using flowing water
words.example: Hydroelectric dams provide clean power.

words.definitionEn: relating to heat from the earth
words.example: Geothermal energy is harnessed from underground heat.

words.definitionEn: organic matter used as fuel
words.example: Biomass can be burned for heat or electricity.

words.definitionEn: natural fuel formed from ancient organisms
words.example: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide.

words.definitionEn: not replaceable once used
words.example: Oil is a non-renewable resource.

words.definitionEn: the act of using resources
words.example: Energy consumption has risen sharply.

words.definitionEn: the ability to do something without waste
words.example: Improving energy efficiency reduces costs.

words.definitionEn: the production and discharge of something, especially gas
words.example: Carbon emissions contribute to global warming.

words.definitionEn: gases that trap heat in the atmosphere
words.example: Methane is a potent greenhouse gas.

words.definitionEn: amount of carbon dioxide produced by an activity
words.example: Reducing your carbon footprint helps the environment.

words.definitionEn: able to be maintained over time
words.example: Sustainable energy sources are vital for the future.

words.definitionEn: network for transmitting electricity
words.example: The power grid supplies electricity to homes.

words.definitionEn: machine for generating power from moving fluid
words.example: Wind turbines are common in rural areas.

words.definitionEn: converting light into electricity
words.example: Photovoltaic cells are used in solar panels.

words.definitionEn: material that prevents heat loss
words.example: Proper insulation reduces heating costs.

words.definitionEn: careful use of resources
words.example: Energy conservation is essential for sustainability.

words.definitionEn: reduction in quantity
words.example: The depletion of oil reserves is a concern.

words.definitionEn: designed to use less energy
words.example: Energy-saving appliances reduce electricity bills.

words.definitionEn: requiring a lot of energy to operate
words.example: Energy-intensive industries need to adopt cleaner technologies.

words.definitionEn: a period of severe shortage of energy supply
words.example: The energy crisis led to higher prices and power cuts.

words.definitionEn: uninterrupted availability of energy sources at an affordable price
words.example: Diversifying energy sources improves energy security.

words.definitionEn: energy that does not pollute the environment
words.example: Governments should invest more in clean energy.

words.definitionEn: energy from natural sources that are replenished
words.example: Green energy helps reduce carbon emissions.

words.definitionEn: energy derived from sources other than fossil fuels
words.example: Alternative energy includes solar, wind, and hydro power.

words.definitionEn: energy released from nuclear reactions
words.example: Nuclear energy is a controversial source of power.

words.definitionEn: energy that comes from heat
words.example: Thermal energy from the sun can be used for heating.

words.definitionEn: a facility where electricity is generated
words.example: The coal-fired power plant will be shut down.

words.definitionEn: a machine that converts mechanical energy into electrical energy
words.example: A backup generator provides power during outages.

words.definitionEn: the process of sending electricity over long distances
words.example: High-voltage transmission lines carry electricity across the country.

words.definitionEn: the delivery of electricity to end users
words.example: The distribution network must be upgraded to handle more renewable energy.

words.definitionEn: an electricity network that uses digital technology to manage supply and demand
words.example: A smart grid optimizes energy use and reduces waste.

words.definitionEn: an inspection of energy use to identify savings opportunities
words.example: Conducting an energy audit can lower electricity bills.

words.definitionEn: a statement of charges for energy consumed
words.example: High energy bills are a burden for low-income households.

words.definitionEn: lack of access to modern energy services
words.example: Energy poverty affects millions of people in developing countries.

words.definitionEn: using less fuel to perform a task
words.example: Fuel-efficient vehicles help reduce carbon emissions.

words.definitionEn: achieving net zero carbon emissions
words.example: The company aims to become carbon-neutral by 2050.

words.definitionEn: a tax on the burning of fossil fuels based on carbon content
words.example: A carbon tax incentivizes companies to reduce emissions.

words.meaningVi: danh mục năng lượng tái tạo
words.definitionEn: a set of renewable energy sources used to meet a target
words.example: The state has a renewable portfolio standard requiring 50% clean energy.

words.definitionEn: having no net emissions of greenhouse gases
words.example: Many countries have pledged to achieve net-zero emissions.

words.definitionEn: a shift from fossil fuels to renewable energy
words.example: The global energy transition requires significant investment.

words.definitionEn: the process of reducing carbon emissions
words.example: Decarbonization of the economy is essential for climate goals.

words.definitionEn: the process of powering systems with electricity
words.example: Electrification of transport can reduce reliance on oil.

words.definitionEn: capturing energy for later use
words.example: Energy storage systems are crucial for integrating renewables.

words.definitionEn: a device that stores chemical energy for electrical use
words.example: Lithium-ion batteries are widely used in electric vehicles.

words.definitionEn: a clean fuel that produces water when burned
words.example: Hydrogen fuel cells are a promising clean technology.

words.definitionEn: gas produced from organic waste, used as fuel
words.example: Biogas from landfills can be used to generate electricity.

words.meaningVi: trang trại năng lượng mặt trời
words.definitionEn: a large area of solar panels used to generate electricity
words.example: A large solar farm can power thousands of homes.
